title: Medicare payments in years after the State licence expired
question: Were San Francisco clinicians paid by Medicare in years after the expiry date the State licensing board lists for them?
finding: Of 6,037 San Francisco physicians and nurse practitioners whose federal licence number is in the State files, 27 were paid by Medicare in a data year after their licence's listed expiry, with the licence now lapsed ("delinquent"): $2.2 million in those years. For physicians: 18 of 4,946, $2.0 million. Another 205 gave a licence number the boards' files do not list at all (113 of them paid in 2023 or 2024); the files omit revoked, surrendered and cancelled licences, and some federal entries carry a mistyped number. Nobody is named here.
how: San Francisco individual providers in the Medicare by-provider files (2018-2024). The State licence number is the one each reported to the federal registry (physicians: taxonomy 207 or 208, letter A, C or G and digits; nurse practitioners: taxonomy 363L). Matched to the Medical Board or nursing board file on number. "Paid after expiry" counts providers whose licence is now delinquent and who had Medicare payments in a calendar year after the year of the listed expiry date.
limits: A clinician can renew late and be reinstated with the same number; the file gives only the current expiry date. Medicare data years are years of service, and payments for earlier services can arrive later. A provider may also hold a second licence, practise under a federal post where a State licence is not required, or have reported a wrong number to the federal registry. Individuals are counted, not listed; the names are in the public files and a check would use the board's own lookup.
